doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: What Dizzy said about Charlie Parker and the old days
summary: Dizzy rarely reminisced, but praised Parker, denied seeing him use drugs and mentioned being ripped off at the Three Deuces.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Was he the type of guy, would he talk about “the old days?” His days with Charlie Parker? Did he reminisce about his early career?

Not much, not with me. I remember asking about Charlie Parker and all I remember he said was that when he met Charlie Parker, Charlie was playing that way. So we said, “Hey Dizzy, did you guys work on that?” He said, “No, when we met I was playing that way, and when he came from Kansas City he was playing his way.” He always talked © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

about how great a musician Charlie Parker was, never said anything negative about Charlie Parker. I saw him many times, people coming to him and asking him about if Charlie has any drug problem, he never liked to talk about that, and I remember Dizzy giving the answer that, “I never saw him doing drugs.” So that was Dizzy. He told stories about the past, when they used to play at the Three Deuces in New York, when they used to play there, how they were ripped off, how the people took advantage of them, you know meaning business-wise, that type of thing.
But regarding Charlie Parker he always said that Charlie Parker was one of the greatest musicians he ever met and had the chance to play with.
